From those instructions, if a user selects the feature, it will be applied in app. Some features will require the user to do things or input
  values. For example, increasing the volume of an audio clip requires the user to select a clip, then choose a volume. Running this help script should instruct the user to select a clip, and when they do, open the settings panel for the volume and instruct them to choose a new value. Essentially I want to build
  tutorial walkthroughs for everything. We can also use them to create instructional videos for later.
  This is obviously a huge amount of work, so I'd like to pick a handful of features to model this feature with. Then we can test and iterate.

# Frame Job User Guide

Frame Job is a native macOS video editor for Apple Silicon Macs running
macOS 26 or later. You open a movie, arrange it on layered tracks over a fixed
canvas, then trim, cut, grade, caption, animate and export it. Every edit you
make in the window can also be made by an AI agent over MCP, or by the built-in
Assistant.

The quickest way in: **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a movie makes an untitled project
sized and timed to it, with the movie on Track 1, ready to cut. Save writes a
`.framejob` package.

## The pages

Read the first four in order to learn the editor; the rest stand alone.

1. [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md) — starting, saving and opening projects, the `.framejob` package, the Document tab's canvas settings, importing files, the Media tab and relinking.
2. [The timeline and playback](timeline.md) — the editor window, tracks and their switches, the ruler and playhead, zoom, selection, snapping, markers, the in/out range and playback.
3. [Editing clips](editing.md) — placing, moving, trimming, slipping, splitting, deleting and closing gaps, copy and paste, and nests.
4. [Canvas, layers, text and shapes](canvas-and-layers.md) — placing a picture on the canvas, opacity, blend modes, shadows and filters, text, shape, image and background clips, and matte tracks.
5. [Motion, actions and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) — actions that animate a clip's properties over time, motion presets, and transitions between clips.
6. [Speed, reverse and freeze frames](speed.md) — constant speed, fitting a clip to a length, rate stretch, speed ramps and their presets, reversing and freeze frames.
7. [Audio](audio.md) — clip levels, fades, ducking, noise reduction, compression, pan, mute and solo, Normalize and Synchronize Audio.
8. [Remove Silences and Remove Filler Words](cleanup-tools.md) — cutting dead air and filler words out of a spoken recording in one step.
9. [Captions and transcription](captions.md) — importing and exporting captions, and transcribing speech on this Mac or with AssemblyAI into subtitles or word-by-word captions.
10. [Colour grading](color-grading.md) — the Color tab, wheels, curves, looks and LUTs, adjustment clips and qualifiers, Show Ungraded and the scopes.
11. [HDR and colour management](hdr-and-color.md) — how sources are read, camera log, SDR and HDR (HLG) projects, blending, and HDR and SDR deliverables.
12. [Motion graphics](graphics.md) — graphic clips, the built-in graphics, their properties in the inspector, and bringing in your own.
13. [Screen recording](screen-recording.md) — recording a display or a window with system audio, microphone and click rings, recording a camera on its own or beside the screen, and recording voice-overs.
14. [Exporting](export.md) — the export sheet, its formats and settings, presets, the Export Queue, and saving single frames.
15. [The Assistant](assistant.md) — chatting with Claude in the inspector to edit the open project, on your own Anthropic key.
16. [Driving Frame Job from an AI agent (MCP)](mcp.md) — connecting an MCP client such as Claude Code, how calls behave, and every tool.
17. [Settings](settings.md) — the Settings window, updates (Check for Updates… in the downloaded copy), the View choices Frame Job remembers, and where it keeps its files.
18. [Menus and keyboard shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md) — every menu command with its shortcut, and the keys, gestures and context menus that have no menu item.

Writing your own graphic module is covered by the
[graphics API reference](../graphics-api.md).

# Audio

Frame Job mixes sound from every clip that has it: a camera clip, an audio-only file, a microphone recording or a nest. Each clip has its own level, fades, ducking, noise reduction, compressor, pan and mono fold, and each track can be muted or soloed. Two commands do the measuring for you. Normalize sets a clip's level from its loudest moment, and Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by their sound. The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written.

## Where audio lives

There is only one kind of track. Any track can hold a clip with sound, whether it is a video file, an audio-only file (a voice-over, music, a recorder's take) or a clip you split off with Detach Audio. A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline.

The waveform shows the level of the file itself, so moving the Volume slider doesn't redraw it. It's drawn faded when the clip is muted, when its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track that holds only sound clips is drawn as a shorter lane than a track with pictures.

When the selection includes at least one clip that plays sound, the Clip tab of the inspector shows a **Sound** sub-tab. A clip counts as having sound when its file has an audio track and its audio is switched on, or when it is a nest that holds audio. The Sound sub-tab has six sections, in this order:

1. **Volume**: level, gain read-out, Mute and Normalize
2. **Fades**: fade in and fade out
3. **Ducking**: lowers every other clip while this one plays
4. **Noise Reduction**
5. **Compressor**
6. **Mix**: pan, mix to mono and Detach Audio

Noise Reduction, Compressor and Mix appear in the order the sound passes through them. Volume, the fades and ducking are applied last, like a fader.

Every section header has a summary and a Reset button that appears when the section differs from its default. The summaries read:

| Section | Summary |
|---|---|
| Volume | "muted", "silent" (at 0 %), or the gain, for example "+3.5 dB" |
| Fades | both lengths, for example "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none" |
| Ducking | the duck level, for example "20%", or "off" |
| Noise Reduction | the amount, for example "50%", or "off" |
| Compressor | the ratio, for example "3.0:1", or "off" |
| Mix | "centre", "mono", or the pan position, for example "left 40" |

 When you change a control with several clips selected, the change goes to all of them. A control whose clips hold different values is marked mixed.

### Sound on a nest

A nest clip has the same Sound sub-tab, but not every control reaches the clips inside it:

- **Volume, Mute and the fades** on a nest clip scale everything inside it. Turning a nest down turns all of it down, and muting it silences all of it.
- **Mix to mono** on a nest clip folds the nest's whole mix.
- **Ducking** on a nest clip lowers the rest of the project for the nest's whole length.
- **Pan, the compressor and noise reduction** set on a nest clip have no effect. Open the nest (⌘↓) and set them on the clips inside.

*Agents:* `set_audio` (`clips`, `patch`) changes any of these properties on one or more clips. Its patch keys are `volume`, `muted`, `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `duck`, `mono`, `keep_pitch`, `pan`, `compressor` and `noise_reduction`. Setting `duck` or `compressor` to null turns it off. `get_project` reads them back.

## Volume

| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | The clip's level as a percentage. Quick picks: 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 400. | 0–400 % | 100 % |
| Gain | Read-only: the volume in dB (for example "+6.0 dB"), or "silent" at 0 %. | — | +0.0 dB |
| Mute | Silences the clip without changing its volume. | on / off | off |
| Normalize | Sets the volume from the clip's own loudest moment (see below). | — | — |

The section's summary reads "muted", "silent" or the gain in dB. Reset puts the volume back to 100 % and turns Mute off.

You can animate volume, Mute and the fades with actions. While an action is selected, the Volume row, the Mute checkbox and the Fade in and Fade out rows write that action's end state, so a level moves across the action's span. Pan, Mix to mono, Keep pitch, the compressor, noise reduction and ducking can't be animated. They always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected.

  level until the tool sets `normal`. `tools/proof/graphic_memory_proof.py`
  drives it.
- `PlaybackTrial.swift` — `PlaybackTrials`, `play_preview`'s record (dev
  only): `Compositor.serve` reports each finished frame's time, compose
  time and, while a trial asks, a SHA-256 of the destination's pixels;
  `recorded(_:)` copies a running trial's record without ending it.
- `AgentServer+MenuItem.swift` — `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet`
  (road map 11's V2b, dev only, wholly under the flag). It runs a main-menu
  item by path in a NAMED project window's own responder chain, never
  nil-targeted, and works with the app inactive and the window occluded
  (measured, V2b's D rows). It refuses by name an item that is disabled, a
  submenu, `framework`, `modal` or unclassified, and one whose own target does
  not answer its action. It answers after a settle:
  reads 20 ms apart, answered on 5 equal, bounded at 3 s. The answer's
  `sheet_at_return` says whether a sheet was attached when the action
  returned, read in the perform's own hop. `cancel_sheet` closes an attached
  sheet through its own Cancel, and refuses a file panel with no parent window
  in its own words (unreachable as far as known). Both run off main
  (`devOffMainTools`), and every AppKit touch is an `onMain` hop.
- `UIMenu.swift` — the menu tool's main-thread half. It walks the menu's
  leaves and looks up a path, validating each level first because a
  validator may retitle an item, and filling each level by its delegate for
  the named window first (`fillDynamic`: Clip ▸ Look ▸'s LUT rows). It holds the refusal, an ALLOW table where
  a selector with no row is `unclassified`, and the responder walk and
  validation, which never write `isEnabled`. An item's explicit target counts
  only when it answers the action; otherwise the item has no target and is
  disabled, as AppKit greys it, with no fallback to the chain (#133,
  `v2_menu.py` H5). It performs through
  `ProjectDocument.inUndoGroupIfRegistered`: an item's edits are one step
  (M3); an item that registers nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167,
  `v2_menu.py` U2); an `NSText` target keeps the eager group except for
  `copy:` and `selectAll:`, which change no text (#176, `v2_menu.py` U3); a
  target whose own `undoManager` is not the document's — the Assistant
  composer, and every field editor, which answers its own
  `NSCellUndoManager` — gets no eager group, and on a `ProjectDocument` runs
  in `inUndoGroupIfRegistered`, so its Cut and Paste leave no empty step and a
  document edit it commits is one step (#184, `menu_undo_probe.py` M1, M2, V1,
  F1).
- `UIMenuTable.swift` — `UIMenu.verdicts`, one row per selector, a mirror of
  `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json` in its order. `v2_menu.py`'s H2
  holds the two together, and H1 holds the inventory to the live menu, so a
  new menu item needs a row in both.
- `UISheet.swift` — the settle fingerprint (the attached sheet, the modal
  window, the visible window numbers) and the Cancel: a file panel is ended
  with `.cancel`, otherwise the Escape button is pressed, otherwise a lone
  button.
- `AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift` — `select_inspector_tab` (road map 11's
  V3, dev only, wholly under the flag). It picks the inspector's tab and the
  Clip tab's sub-tab through `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and
  `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the strips' own click paths, so a `snapshot_ui`
  capture is what a click shows. It runs on MAIN, not in `devOffMainTools`.
  With no tab it changes nothing, and answers the tab, the active sub-tab
  and the sub-tabs on offer. `section` scrolls a section into view, and the
  answer's `look_thumbnails_pending` says the gallery is still rendering (GR-7).
  Every refusal leaves the inspector as it was.
- `EditorViewController+Look.swift` — Clip ▸ Look ▸ (the eight, a separator,
  None; a checkmark or a dash; spec §11 GR-7) and its validator arm; the
  dev-only launch default `-RCDevLookGalleryDump <folder>` writes each set of
  thumbnails as PNGs for the proof.
- `DevAppearance.swift` — `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, a dev-only launch
  default (road map 11's V3). It sets `NSApp.appearance` from `main.swift`
  before `NSApplicationMain`, so every view is built in that look. A live
  switch leaves colours taken at build time in the launch look, which is why
  `snapshot_ui` refuses `appearance` and names this default instead.
- `AgentServer+Assistant.swift` — `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer`
  (road map 12 A1, dev only, wholly under the flag). Both run off main
  (`devOffMainTools`): one `onMain` resolves the target, the editor and the
  session and sends, answers or stops; then the wait for "not busy" runs
  INSIDE `AgentLane.releasingLock`, polling the phase every 50 ms, because
  the turn's own calls need the lock. The target is resolved BEFORE the
  release, never inside it, where an assistant call may hold
  `callDocument`. `assistant_answer` never opens a session. The answer is
  the state, the question, the text deltas joined and the other events since
  the call — never the key or the model, each `cost` passed through
  `AssistantSpend.toolView` (road map 13 P2). `assistant_send` without `pane`
  sends through `EditorViewController.assistantSend`, so the transcript gets
  the person's line; with `pane` (road map 12 A2) both tools go through the
  Assistant tab's own controls — the composer (its `string` set, any marked
  text committed first) and a `performClick` on Send,
  Allow's or Deny's `mouseDown` with a synthesized click at its centre, Send
  while it reads Stop — refused by name, changing nothing, when the control
  is not in a window or is hidden. The pane check comes before the session
  opens, and the idle check before the click, so a pane send never clicks
  Stop. `stop_after` (seconds, 0.1…600 and less than `timeout`; on
  `assistant_answer` only with `allow`) presses Stop once inside the wait,
  through `editor.assistantStop()`, when the turn is still busy or asking, and
  the answer carries `stopped_ms` (else null).
- `DevAssistantLaunch.swift` — `-RCDevAssistantSend <text>
  -RCDevAssistantReport <path>`, a dev-only launch default (road map 12 A1),
  both from the argument domain alone: after launch, one turn in an untitled
  project with or without the MCP server, a `get_project` through the lane,
  one atomic JSON report (its events' `cost`s through
  `AssistantSpend.toolView`, road map 13 P2), and the session closed. One key
  alone is one stderr line. Installed from `main.swift` after `DevAppearance.apply()`.
- `AgentServer+Snapshot.swift` — `snapshot_ui` (road map 11's V2a, dev only,
  wholly under the flag). It lists the windows, or captures the editor (whole
  or a region), an attached sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel through `cacheDisplay`:
  an image block plus JSON and a PNG, with a `<name>.layout.json` beside it.
  It runs OFF main (`devOffMainTools`): the fill renders through
  `Exporter.renderFrameReported`, the settle sleeps between passes, and every
  AppKit touch is an `onMain` hop. A `defer` unstages on every exit. It works
  with the app inactive and its window occluded (measured, V2a's O rows).
  `appearance` is refused, naming `-RCDevAppearance`.
- `UISnapshot.swift` — `snapshot_ui`'s main-thread half. It resolves the
  window (Settings, Welcome and the recorder panel found in `NSApp.windows`
  by controller class, never `.shared`, which would build them) and the regions (the root's `BarView` and the three pane
  containers), holds the window facts and the listing, and stages the fill
  as an `NSImageView` just above
  `playerHost`, under `safeGuides` and `overlay` (V1's W4a). It also runs one
  `cacheDisplay` pass. `kind(of:)` and `row(_:)` are internal, not private,
  because the menu tool's result rows use them.

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into

# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.

# Walkthroughs — draft road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: DRAFT for the owner's review (2026-10-31). Nothing is built and no
decision below is recorded in spec §11 yet; TU0 records them.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model walkthroughs** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Walkthroughs are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The walkthrough dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Walkthroughs get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Walkthrough**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project. The
word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: tutorial (which suggests a
separate course with its own sample material), wizard (which suggests the
app makes the choices).

**Step**: one numbered item in a walkthrough. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
Me does.

## 4. The shape

### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list

A walkthrough is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Walkthrough:`
heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

```markdown
### Walkthrough: change a clip's volume
<!-- walkthrough {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
```

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every walkthrough into one `Walkthroughs.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

### 4.2 The step vocabulary

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.
Every key is optional except that a step has a sentence.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the walkthrough does not require this step. |

Variables: `$selection` (the clip ids when the step began), `$created`
(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip
in time order that matches, for a Show Me that has to choose a clip).

### 4.3 The runner and the coach panel

- **The coach panel.** A small non-activating floating panel beside the
  editor window, the same kind of panel as the recorder. It shows the title,
  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.
- **The spotlight.** A borderless, click-through child window over the
  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when
  the layout moves. Because it is a window, it sits above the Metal and
  `AVPlayerLayer` layers.
- **Needs.** Before step 1, the walkthrough's `needs` are checked against the
  open project. When they are not met, the panel says what is missing and
  how to get it, for example "This walkthrough needs a clip with sound. Open
  a movie first (File ▸ Open…)", and does not start.
- **Where to start one.** **Help ▸ Walkthroughs ▸** has one submenu per guide
  page, filled from `Walkthroughs.json`. A "Try it in Frame Job" link from
  the online guide (`framejob://walkthrough/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

### 4.4 Show Me

Show Me runs the step's `show_me` through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
the Assistant's calls take. Each Show Me edit is an ordinary undo step, and
exiting a walkthrough undoes nothing. Show Me does three jobs:

- it helps a person who is stuck;
- it lets a proof run every walkthrough to the end with no person present;
- it is what auto-play will use for the videos (§8).

## 5. What stays out of the model phase

- Rolling walkthroughs out to every guide page, and the worked examples each
  page still lacks (after TU4, one batch per page).
- A bundled practice project. The model walkthroughs run on the person's
  own project and check `needs` first.
- Auto-play and video capture (§8).
- The `framejob://` link (#385).

## 6. The model set

Five walkthroughs, chosen so that between them they use every step shape the
design has. If these five work, the remaining walkthroughs need content
only, not new machinery.

| # | Walkthrough (guide page) | Steps | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Change a clip's volume** (`audio.md`) | select a clip with sound → Sound ▸ Volume opens → change the level → play | the owner's example: a selection wait, a sub-tab and section reveal, a value-changed wait |
| 2 | **Split a clip** (`editing.md`) | select a clip → move the playhead into it → Clip ▸ Split (⌘T) | a playhead wait (the person scrubs), a menu or key action, a count wait, `$created` |
| 3 | **Add a title** (`canvas-and-layers.md`) | press T or the bar's Add Text → type the words in Text ▸ Content → drag it on the canvas | a bar-button spotlight, a new clip the next step follows, text entry while the panel is up, a canvas gesture (`changed: video.position`) |
| 4 | **Cross-dissolve two clips** (`motion-and-transitions.md`) | select the later of two clips that meet → Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve → set its length in the Transition section | `needs` that the project may not meet, a submenu item, a section that only exists once the edit has applied |
| 5 | **Export a range** (`export.md`) | set In and Out (I, O) → File ▸ Export… → pick a format in the sheet → Export | view-state waits (`range`), a sheet and spotlights inside it (the export sheet has no accessibility ids today), an outcome that is not an edit (`queued`) |

Swaps if the owner prefers: **Remove Silences** (a sheet plus an analysis
wait) for 5, or **Zoom in with an action** (the action lane) for 3.

## 7. Verification

- **`make test`, no app:** `tools/proof/walkthrough_check.py` reads every
  guide page. It checks the following and fails on anything unknown, naming
  the page and step:
  - each walkthrough's JSON against §4.2's vocabulary;
  - each `show_me` tool name and argument key against the build's catalog
    snapshot;
  - each `section:` id and target name against the names the app publishes;
  - each menu path a sentence names against
    `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`;
  - each `changed` path against the schema.
- **Over MCP:** dev tools `walkthrough_start {id}`, `walkthrough_state`,
  `walkthrough_step {action: show_me|next|back|skip}` and
  `walkthrough_exit`, compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`.
  `tools/proof/walkthrough_proof.py` runs each model walkthrough three ways:
  - **as a person:** it meets each wait with the ordinary tools
    (`set_selection`, `set_audio`, `set_playhead`, `perform_menu_item`, …)
    and reads that the runner advanced and that the inspector shows the
    revealed tab, sub-tab and section (`select_inspector_tab` with no tab);
  - **by Show Me alone:** it runs every step's Show Me to the end and reads
    the project back with `get_project`;
  - **with `needs` unmet:** on an empty project it reads the panel's
    sentence.
- **Seeing it:** `snapshot_ui` learns the coach panel as a window kind; a
  capture of the editor with the spotlight up, in both looks.
- **`docs/manual-checks.md` rows:**
  - the ring sits on the right control and follows a window resize and an
    inspector scroll;
  - the panel never takes typing from a field;
  - a person completes each of the five by hand.

## 8. Videos (after TU4, recorded here so the format allows for them)

Every step that has a `show_me` can run unattended. Auto-play performs the
step, holds for a reading time based on the sentence's length, and moves on,
with the coach panel serving as the caption. The recorder (with Include
Frame Job windows) or `screencapture` films it. One question is left for
that phase: a tool call doesn't move the pointer, so a video may want Show
Me performed through the UI instead (the menu item, a synthesized click on
the control). The format doesn't need to change for that; only the
performer does.

## 9. Phases

Each phase is gated, committed and merged on its own
(`feature-worktree-merge-per-phase`).

- **TU0 — decisions and words.** Write
  `designs/spec/11-decisions/walkthroughs.md`: TU-1 one source (the guide's
  list plus HTML-comment halves), TU-2 the closed vocabulary and its checker,
  TU-3 Show Me through `AgentServer.execute` with ordinary undo, TU-4 the
  non-activating panel and the click-through spotlight window, TU-5 `needs`
  checked before step 1 and no practice project in the model phase. Add the
  index row and the `CONTEXT.md` term.
- **TU1 — the five as text, plus the checker.** Write the five walkthroughs
  into their pages; their sentences are useful to a reader before any app
  code exists. Also: the extractor, the bundle step, the app's target-name
  table, and `walkthrough_check.py` in `make test`.
- **TU2 — the runner, with no chrome.** The model, the condition evaluator,
  variables, reveal and Show Me, the dev tools, and `walkthrough_proof.py`'s
  person and Show Me runs over the five.
- **TU3 — the chrome.** The coach panel, the spotlight, Help ▸
  Walkthroughs, the export sheet's ids, `snapshot_ui`'s panel kind, the
  `needs` run, the manual-checks rows, and the guide's page on walkthroughs
  plus its `menus-and-shortcuts.md` row.
- **TU4 — the owner's trial.** The owner runs the five. What they change is
  fixed here, and the decision whether to roll out (and in what order) is
  made here.

## 10. Questions for the owner

1. **The model set:** the five in §6, or with a swap?
2. **Practice material:** the person's own project (recommended for the
   model phase), or a bundled practice project now? A practice project is
   also what the videos will want later.
3. **The word:** "Walkthroughs" in the Help menu, or "Tutorials"?

## Record

(Each phase's record goes here: what landed, what was measured, what the
review found, what is owed.)

# litecode

You are the orchestrator. You do almost no work yourself. You dispatch one subagent at a time, in a fixed order, and check stop conditions between stages. Never spawn two agents at once. Never spawn an agent not listed below. Never explore the codebase yourself — that is the designer's job.

## Setup

1. Derive `<repo-name>` from the git remote or the directory name, and `<task-slug>` from the request (kebab-case, ≤6 words, append `-2`, `-3` if it exists).
2. `HANDOFF=~/.claude/litecode/<repo-name>/<task-slug>/`. Create it. Write the user's verbatim request to `$HANDOFF/request.md`.
3. `TEMPLATES=<this skill's base directory>/references/`, using the base directory shown when this skill loaded. Use that absolute path; never search the filesystem for it.
4. If the user said `litecode resume <task-slug>`, skip to **Resume**.

Every dispatch prompt has the same shape: one or two lines telling the agent the `$HANDOFF` path and which files to read. Dispatches to agents that write from a template also give the `$TEMPLATES` path. Do not paste file contents into the prompt; the agent reads them.

Print exactly one line at each stage transition, e.g. `triage → full route`, `design done → adversary`. Nothing else until the final summary.

## Pipeline

### Stage 0 — triage (`lc-triage`) — always runs

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read request.md. Write 00-triage.md.`

Read `00-triage.md`. If `route: small` → go to Stage 3. If `route: full` → Stage 1.

### Stage 1 — design (`lc-designer`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read request.md and 00-triage.md. Explore the repo as needed. Write 01-spec.md using the spec template.`

Check for `STOP:` in the spec. If present, halt (see **Stopping**).

### Stage 2 — adversary (`lc-adversary`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and only the files it names. Write 02-objections.md.`

Read the verdict line. If `verdict: proceed` and there are zero objections, copy `01-spec.md` to `03-spec-final.md` and go to Stage 3.

### Stage 1b — final design (`lc-designer`)

Dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 01-spec.md and 02-objections.md. Write 03-spec-final.md: the revised spec plus an "Objections addressed" section.`

### Stage 3 — implement (`lc-implementer`)

Full route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read 03-spec-final.md. Implement it. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Small route dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read request.md and 00-triage.md. No spec exists; implement the request directly, touching only files_likely_touched unless you justify otherwise in your notes. Write 04-impl-notes.md and 04-checks.txt.`

Check for `STOP:` in the notes. If present, halt.

### Stage 4 — review (`lc-reviewer`)

**Skip check first.** Run `git diff --stat` (or the equivalent for the repo's VCS). If total changed lines < 80 AND `04-checks.txt` shows every verification command passing (a command recorded as `SKIPPED:` with a reason counts as passing) → skip to **Finish**.

Otherwise dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, and the git diff. Write 05-review.md.`

If `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If `verdict: fix-required` → Stage 5.

### Stage 5 — fix loop (`lc-fixer`, then `lc-reviewer`), at most 5 passes

Fix pass `N` runs from 1 to 5. The review it answers is `05-review.md` for pass 1, and `07-review-N.md` (the re-review written after pass `N-1`) after that.

1. Fix dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Read <that review> and the git diff. Fix every blocker and should-fix. Re-run the spec's verification commands that your fixes can affect. Write 06-fix-notes-N.md.`
2. If the fix notes contain `STOP:`, halt (see **Stopping**).
3. Re-review dispatch: `Handoff dir: $HANDOFF. Templates dir: $TEMPLATES. Read 03-spec-final.md (or request.md on the small route), 04-impl-notes.md, 04-checks.txt, every 06-fix-notes-*.md so far, the review pass N answered, and the git diff. Write 07-review-<N+1>.md.`
4. If that review says `verdict: pass` → **Finish**. If it says `fix-required` and `N < 5` → run pass `N+1`. If `N = 5` → do NOT run the fixer again. Go to **Finish** and report the unresolved findings.

**Stop early** if a re-review lists a blocker or should-fix that the previous review also raised (the same finding at the same file:line) and the fix notes claim it fixed. Go to **Finish** and report that finding as stuck. A sixth pass won't fix what two passes couldn't.

## Stopping

Any stage may write `STOP: <reason>` at the top of its output file. When you see it: halt, tell the user the reason, list the handoff files that exist, and ask how to proceed. Do not try to work around it yourself.

## Resume

List `$HANDOFF`. Restart from the first stage whose output file is missing, following the same routing rules. If `00-triage.md` says `small`, the missing spec files are expected — go by the small route. In the fix loop, the pass number is one more than the count of `06-fix-notes-*.md` already written. If the newest file is a fix note with no `07-review-*.md` after it, run that pass's re-review first. A handoff dir from before the loop (`06-fix-notes.md`, `07-review-2.md`) counts as pass 1.

## Finish

Print a summary, in this order, nothing extra:

- Route: small / full
- Stages run (including how many fix passes)
- Files changed (from `git diff --stat`)
- Verification: pass / fail, with the failing command names if any
- Objections the designer declined (from `03-spec-final.md`), one line each, if any
- Unresolved review findings (blockers / should-fix), if any
- Handoff dir path

## Rules you must not break

- One agent at a time. Sequential only.
- No agent outside the six defined. No ad-hoc "let me just check" subagents.
- Never skip triage.
- Never run more than 5 fix passes, and never run a fix pass without a `fix-required` review in front of it.
- Never paste handoff file contents into dispatch prompts — pass paths.
- You do not read source files. If you're tempted to, you're doing the designer's job at the wrong effort level.

# Orchestrator objection (a fourth, beside 02-objections.md)

**4. correctness / missing-edge-case — a saved practice copy must not point
into the app bundle.** 01-spec.md accepts, as TU-7's risk, that a saved copy's
media resolve to the files inside `Frame Job.app` and break only if the app
moves. That case is commoner than it reads:

- **App Translocation.** A first-run person who opens the downloaded app
  from `~/Downloads` (or from the DMG) without moving it runs it from a
  randomised read-only path under `/private/var/folders/…/AppTranslocation/`,
  new on each launch. The practice project is exactly what a first-run person
  opens, so their saved copy's media links break on the next launch.
- **Updates and moves.** Sparkle replaces the bundle; a person may move or
  rename the app; a later version may change or drop a practice file.

**Fix (recommended):** a practice copy owns its media once it has a file —
the first save of a practice copy (Save, Save As, and `new_project
{practice: true, path: …}`) copies the practice media into the saved package
(the existing Consolidate machinery, or the same copy it does; the media are
a few MB), so the saved project references only files inside itself. Record
it in TU-7 instead of the accepted risk, and add a proof row that the saved
package's media paths are inside the saved package and that it reopens with
no missing media after the bundled copy is out of reach (e.g. its paths
checked not to start with the app bundle's path).

# Orchestrator objections (beside 02-objections.md)

**A. missing-edge-case — a wait already met when its step is reached FORWARD
must advance.** 01-spec.md checks a wait only after a trigger, never when
its step begins, so Back stays where it lands. Forward is different: a
person who starts Change a clip's volume with a clip with sound already
selected is told "Select a clip that has sound" and nothing happens until
they reselect it — the commonest way into that tutorial reads as broken.
Likewise Split's playhead step when the playhead already sits inside the
selected clip, and Export a range's range step when a range is already set.
`changed` waits are unaffected (their baseline is taken at step entry, so
they are never met at entry).

**Fix (recommended):** evaluate the wait once on entry when the step is
reached by advancing, Next, Skip or start (after its `reveal` and baselines,
on the next main-loop turn like any trigger, held while a Show Me list
runs); never on entry by Back. Say it in TU-8, and add proof rows: the
volume tutorial started with a sound clip already selected advances past
step 1 with no further call; Back onto a met step does not advance.

**B. owner choice, and a correctness edge — Show Me's export never
overwrites.** Show Me answering Allow for Export a range is fine (the person
pressed Show Me on a step that says to export; keep the owner choice's
recommendation), but `~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4` may already exist
from an earlier run or be the person's own file. Show Me must write to a
free name (`Frame Job Tutorial 2.mp4`, …, the way the app already picks
free names, if it has such a helper) rather than overwrite or be refused,
and the answer/state must carry the path it wrote so TU3's panel can say
where the file went. The proof then needs no "fail if the file exists" row:
it reads the path from the answer and deletes exactly that file.

  **What changed, by objection:**
  
  1. **Adversary 1 (the Show Me hold mutant):** I added row H1 and moved the mutant to it from M-canvas.add_title.
     - Setup: `add_track`, `add_text_clip`, select that clip, then `tutorial_start canvas.add_title`. Step 1's `clips added` wait is unmet, so it stays on step 1.
     - `show_me` must then land on step 2 with `selection_at_start == created == [the new clip]`.
     - Without the hold, the wait is met after `add_text_clip`, so the step advances early and its baseline holds the clip that was selected before.
     - Objection A's forward-entry evaluation does not hide this. Step 1's wait is unmet at entry, and entry evaluations are held while a Show Me runs.
  
  2. **Adversary 2 (Export sheet left open):** M-export.range now runs `cancel_sheet` after the export and before the close. Every row also fails if its `close_project` is refused.
  
  3. **Adversary 3 (reveal opens nothing):**
     - `InspectorViewController.reveal` calls the section's own `InspectorSection.reveal()` (`InspectorSection.swift:125`, writes no preference) before scrolling.
     - `select_inspector_tab` gains `expanded_sections`, and `expandedSectionIDs()` is added to the interfaces. The dev tool's own `section` scroll still opens nothing.
     - The check is P-transitions.cross_dissolve. `video.transition` is collapsed by default and is not the Clip sub-tab's first section; that first section is the one `ClipPane.swift:250` opens by default. The row records whether the section was collapsed before the reveal.
     - `audio.volume` cannot carry this check, because it is the first section on the Sound sub-tab and opens by default.
     - The proof does not collapse a section itself, because toggling writes a preference a proof may not move.
     - Limit: this mutant is only killed where the section starts collapsed. The spec says so and requires the Debug run (the proofs' own defaults domain) to show it.
  
  4. **Orchestrator A (a wait already met on forward entry):**
     - A forward entry is now a trigger: start, Next, Skip, or an advance by a met wait (`TutorialEntry.forward|back`). It is evaluated on the next main turn and held during a Show Me. Back schedules no evaluation.
     - Cascades follow from this, and a step with no wait never advances by evaluation.
     - New row F1: select Dawn, `tutorial_start audio.volume` answers step 1, and the next `tutorial_state` answers step 2 with `completed [{step:1, by:wait}]`. This relies on main-queue FIFO, which is stated in Approach 8.
     - B1 is now "Back onto a met step stays put".
     - The old mutant "evaluate at step begin" became "evaluate on Back entry too" (B1), and "no forward-entry evaluation" (F1) is new.
